section2: For food production directors, port terminal managers and cold-store duty holders in Wisbech, compliance with the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER) is a strict statutory obligation. Under PUWER Regulation 5, employers must ensure that all storage equipment—whether holding chilled produce at Algores Way Industrial Estate, timber packs at the Port of Wisbech, or clinical archives at North Cambridgeshire Hospital—is maintained in an efficient state, in efficient working order and in good repair. Because pallet and cantilever racking is exposed to continuous mechanical handling collisions, heavy dynamic loading and damp coastal conditions that can cause dangerous deterioration, PUWER Regulation 6 requires periodic inspections at suitable intervals by a competent person, with formal written records retained. The Health and Safety Executive's authoritative guidance document HSG76, Warehousing and Storage: A Guide to Health and Safety, defines the mandatory three-tier inspection hierarchy required to satisfy PUWER. First, warehouse operatives and forklift drivers must report any rack collision or visible structural defect immediately. Second, an appointed Person Responsible for Racking Safety (PRRS) must perform and log regular internal visual checks, normally weekly. Third, an annual expert inspection must be conducted by an independent specialist such as a SEMA Approved Racking Inspector. Failing to uphold this regime in Wisbech's agri-food, port and logistics sectors risks HSE Prohibition Notices, invalidated insurance and prosecution.
section3: During a SEMA racking inspection in Wisbech, our SARI-qualified engineer conducts a thorough structural assessment of every pallet rack, drive-in lane, cantilever stand and shelving bay, grading each defect under SEMA's traffic-light risk system. Using a one-metre straightedge on impacted upright columns and frame bracing, we verify whether deformations fall within SEMA's maximum permissible limits of 3 millimetres in the down-aisle plane, 5 millimetres in the cross-aisle plane and 10 millimetres on horizontal or diagonal bracing struts. Components within these thresholds are graded Green, confirming they remain safe for normal working loads while being documented for monitoring at the next annual cycle. Where frame or bracing damage exceeds those limits, or where essential components such as beam locking pins or floor anchor bolts are missing without creating an immediate danger of collapse, the defect is classified as Amber; under SEMA protocols, Amber bays must be unloaded within four weeks so certified manufacturer replacement parts can be installed, and any Amber defect left loaded beyond twenty-eight days automatically escalates to a Red hazard. Critical damage—including deflections exceeding twice the SEMA limit, buckled upright profiles or disengaged beam connectors—is classified as Red, requiring immediate offloading and physical isolation of the bay. Our comprehensive written report includes bay-by-bay defect locations, load notice audits and compliance guidance referencing https://www.rackstor.co.uk/sema-racking-inspection-checklist.

section2: Every heavy engineering and pipework fabricator, medical packaging manufacturer, electronics distributor, third-party logistics warehouse, and public healthcare or borough council authority operating storage racking in Chesterfield holds strict statutory duties under the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER). section3: In Chesterfield's heavy pipework and engineering warehouses at Sheepbridge Industrial Estate and Whittington Moor or acute clinical and municipal archives at Chesterfield Royal Hospital and Rose Hill, objective SEMA inspection ensures damaged bays are isolated before heavy steel fabrications, medical pallets, or archive boxes trigger a structural collapse. section3: When our SEMA Approved Racking Inspector evaluates a factory store, extrusion yard or cold store in Shropshire, every racking bay and cantilever arm is assessed against SEMA's engineering tolerances and graded using the traffic-light risk system. HSG76 establishes a structured three-tier inspection hierarchy to satisfy these legal duties. First, warehouse operatives and MHE drivers must report any rack impact or structural fault immediately. Across the East Riding of Yorkshire's rail assembly hubs at Goole 36, logistics parks at Melton West and caravan plants in Bridlington and Beverley, non-compliance risks HSE enforcement notices, voided insurance and catastrophic rack failure.
section3: When our SEMA Approved Rack Inspectors audit storage systems across the East Riding of Yorkshire, every defect is classified using SEMA's formal Red, Amber and Green risk grading framework to provide clear engineering priorities. section3: Whether auditing high-bay parcel fulfilment aisles at Houstoun Industrial Estate or GMP vaccine cold stores at Kirkton Campus Business Park, our SEMA Approved Racking Inspectors in Livingston classify every structural measurement under SEMA's Red, Amber, and Green risk protocol.
